title: Printmaking Methods: Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch into reduction lino, etching grounds, lithography and editions.
meta_desc: Stretch GCSE printmaking: reduction printing, etching, lithography, edition numbering.
final_note: Numbering an edition is the artist's signature of integrity.

concepts.def: Multi-colour print using one shrinking block.
Acid bites into a plate where ground is removed.
Print outside the edition, marked A/P.
Fraction showing print number out of total.

walkthroughs.body_html: Reduction printing uses one block. Print the lightest colour first, then cut away the areas you want to keep that colour. Print the next colour over the top. Repeat. Once carved, the block can never reprint that edition.

Cover a metal plate in a waxy ground, draw lines through it, then place the plate in acid. The acid bites only where the ground was removed. Time and acid strength control the line depth. Add aquatint for tonal areas.

Each finished print is numbered as a fraction — "4/20" means the 4th of 20 in the edition. Test prints outside the edition are marked A/P (Artist's Proof). Sign and date prints in pencil under the image.
